newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian merger method a "stroke of genius"-Breuer.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian merger method a "stroke of genius"-Breuer.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG chief Rolf Breuer said on Wednesday the way in which Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG plan to merge is a "stroke of genius."
He said the planned exchange of most of Vereinsbank's stake in Allianz AG for Hypo-Bank deserved respect and admiration provided that it was permitted by tax authorities.

Breuer told Deutsche's half-year news conference that his bank had no fundamental objections to swapping industrial shareholdings for stakes in banks if it was possible to do so in a tax efficient way.
But he added that past experience showed that such swap operations were subject to tight restrictions from fiscal authorities.

A German legal opinion -- known as the Tauschgutachten -- allows two parties to swap assets without incurring 60 percent capital gains tax provided that the assets are of equal value, of equal type and equal function.
Authorities in Munich appear to be a lot looser in their interpretation of the rules than Frankfurt authorities.
The two merging banks are both based in Munich.
